correctness.rationale: All connected chordal graphs are generated by adjoining a simplicial vertex with a nonempty clique neighborhood to a smaller connected chordal graph; disconnecteds by unique component multisets. Exact graph-isomorphism backtracking eliminates duplicates, then stable shared-palette 1-WL on a pair disjoint union tests C^2 equivalence. The inspected deterministic code enumerates 1614 connected and 2119 total chordal isomorphism types at order 8, producing 2117 stable refinement classes, with exactly two doubletons and none below 8. Independent Python/NetworkX graph6 decoding verified both stated 8-vertex pairs are nonisomorphic yet have equal shared-refinement color multisets: the 13-edge 2-tree pair and 14-edge split pair. Complete n=8 census depends on correctness of the inspected finite exhaustive algorithm; full census was not separately rerun in this execution.

originality.rationale: Earlier separate complete results classify the first 2-tree collision (one among 39 eight-vertex 2-trees) and the first split-graph collision (witness eight, onward via universal joins). Their full RESULT.md primary statements were read. Neither classifies all chordal graphs through eight; because chordal graphs strictly contain both subclasses, their two witness classifications do not imply that no third collision exists in the remaining 2119 chordal types. Thus the complete joint first obstruction layer is a distinct, motivated finite census.

It is a useful complete small-order benchmark with explicit graph6 witnesses; makes no claim about n>=9.
